text: 🚨 US INFLATION ACCELERATES — FED HIKE RISK RISES US inflation picked up in August, strengthening the case for another Fed rate hike next week. Headline CPI rose 0.4% M/M and 3.4% Y/Y, while core CPI increased 0.3% M/M. Gasoline was a key driver, with oil back above $100/barrel adding to inflation concerns. Markets had been pricing roughly a 70% chance of a 25bp hike ahead of the report. Higher inflation + resilient employment + elevated oil prices = increasing pressure on the Fed to tighten.

author: WalterBloomberg
text: 🚨 US CPI: Inflation Comes In Hotter Than Expected August US inflation data delivered a firmer-than-expected headline reading, adding another complication to the Federal Reserve outlook. Headline CPI rose 0.396% M/M on an unrounded basis, effectively 0.4%, compared with expectations of around 0.39%. The bigger surprise came from core CPI, which increased 0.290% M/M, versus expectations of around 0.22% and up from 0.215% in the previous month. On a year-over-year basis: Headline CPI: 3.397% Core CPI: 2.446%, down from 2.478% previously The composition is important. Headline inflation is running above 3%, while monthly core inflation accelerated materially. That combination makes the path toward easier monetary policy more difficult, particularly against a backdrop of elevated energy prices and geopolitical risk.

text: Trump Signals Possible US-Canada Trade Deal Soon President Donald Trump said the United States and Canada could reach a trade agreement “fairly soon,” signaling optimism after months of escalating tensions between the two countries. Trump said Canada wants a deal with Washington but insisted that Canadian tariffs on US farmers must be addressed, particularly what he described as duties as high as 400%. The trade dispute has expanded beyond tariffs, threatening cross-border supply chains and industries such as automobiles. After negotiations collapsed in August, both countries imposed additional tariffs and trade restrictions, raising concerns about higher prices and further economic disruption. Despite Trump’s latest comments, formal negotiations have yet to clearly resume, leaving uncertainty over whether the two sides can quickly reach a broader agreement.

text: Trump’s Ireland Visit Highlights Delicate US-Ireland Ties US President Donald Trump arrived in Ireland for a two-day visit, receiving a warm welcome from Irish leaders despite political tensions and public criticism surrounding his presidency. Trump is scheduled to meet Taoiseach Micheál Martin, with trade expected to be a key topic, while his itinerary also includes attending the Irish Open at his family’s golf resort in Doonbeg. Irish officials are seeking to maintain strong relations with Trump as Ireland’s economy remains closely linked to US investment and multinational companies. Although the visit is being presented as an opportunity to highlight longstanding ties between the two countries, disagreements over tariffs, trade balances, defense and US-European relations create diplomatic challenges for Dublin, particularly as Ireland currently holds the rotating presidency of the European Union.

text: BRICS Urges Restraint as Middle East Tensions Escalate BRICS nations, including Iran, the United Arab Emirates, India and China, have expressed deep concern over rising tensions in the Middle East and called for maximum restraint. author: firstsquaw
text: Anthropic CEO Calls for Slower AI Development Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called for the AI industry to slow the pace of developing new models, warning that rapidly advancing AI could create serious risks for humans. He pointed to AI’s growing ability to improve itself and recent incidents in which AI agents breached websites during testing. Amodei said slowing development does not mean stopping AI progress, but giving companies more time to improve safety and allow independent experts to evaluate their systems. He also called for cooperation across the industry and between countries, saying AI can greatly benefit society if it is developed carefully and responsibly.

text: California Diesel Prices Hit Record Highs Diesel prices in California have surged to record levels, with the statewide average rising above $8 a gallon and one San Diego station charging $9.99. Low fuel supplies, reduced refining capacity, limited pipelines and high state taxes are worsening the crisis, while global conflicts are putting further pressure on energy markets. The rising costs are hurting businesses that depend heavily on diesel, including trucking, moving and construction companies. Many are being forced to raise prices or accept lower profits as fuel expenses soar, adding to inflation and making everyday goods and services more expensive for consumers.

text: The biggest issue with an AI "safety slowdown:" What happens with China? While there are legitimate concerns around the safety of AI and how quickly it is evolving, the AI race is global. If US AI giants agree to slow progress and focus on safety, there must be an international agreement in place as well. And, even if there is an agreement in place, how do we regulate compliance? text: SAUDI PIPELINE OUTAGE THREATENS 4% OF GLOBAL OIL SUPPLY Saudi Arabia could lose up to 4 million barrels per day of exports — roughly 4% of global supply — if its critical East-West pipeline does not restart within days, Reuters reports.
